lines.i1: After a wedding, the best photos are stuck on the guests' phones.
lines.i2: And the hall is often a basement, with no signal at all.
lines.i3: This is Mehfil. The wedding's camera, on every guest's phone.
lines.h1: The host makes an event, and gets one QR code for the tables.
lines.g1: A guest scans it. There's no app to install. Just a name, and the camera opens.
lines.g2: Rohit takes three photos. They're sent, and the couple's live wall shows three.
lines.n1: Isha is in the hall, with no signal.
lines.n2: She keeps shooting. Her four photos wait on her phone, and the wall doesn't move.
lines.n4: When the signal comes back, she opens the link again, and the photos send by themselves.
lines.n5: Seven photos taken, seven on the server. Nothing lost.
lines.r1: Until the album opens, nobody can see anyone else's photos. The server enforces that, not the app.
lines.r2: The host opens the album, and every guest sees every photo.
lines.s1: The album can also open by itself, the next morning. That time lives on the server, in the database.
lines.s2: Here, we restarted the live server just before the album was due. It still opened, right on time.
lines.p1: And it's all built on Server pod.
lines.p2: Offline sync keeps each photo's record on the phone. File storage takes the photo. A stream drives the live wall. And the server decides when the album opens.
lines.p3: We tested it on two real phones, in airplane mode. And it's live now, on Server pod Cloud.
